```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(

```

`datasinking` is an R client for the
[DataSinking API](https://datasink.ing), which turns full-text financial
reports — annual, semi-annual and quarterly filings across the US, UK, China,
Japan, Korea, Taiwan and more — into clean, section-addressable Markdown. You
get the MD&A, risk factors and footnotes that line-item APIs don't give you.

## Setup

Get an API key at <https://datasink.ing>, then set it once per session:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(datasinking)
ds_set_key("your-api-key")
```

Every function reads the key from the `DATASINKING_API_KEY` environment
variable, so you can also set it in your `.Renviron`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# ~/.Renviron
DATASINKING_API_KEY=your-api-key
```

## Listing exchanges and stocks

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ds_exchanges()

ds_stocks("szse")
```

`ds_exchanges()` returns a character vector of exchange codes;
`ds_stocks()` returns a data.frame of `stock_code` / `stock_name` /
`report_count`.

## Finding documents

Pass an FMP-style ticker (e.g. `"AAPL"`, `"600519.SS"`, `"7203.T"`) plus an
optional `doc_type` (`"annual"`, `"semiannual"`, `"q1"`, `"q3"`):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
docs <- ds_documents(symbol = "600519.SS", doc_type = "annual")
docs
```

`ds_documents()` returns a data.frame of metadata. The total number of
matching documents is stored as an attribute: `attr(docs, "total")`.

## Reading a report

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Full text as Markdown
doc <- ds_report(id = docs$id[1])
cat(doc$content)

# Just one section (fuzzy title match)
mdna <- ds_report(id = docs$id[1], section = "MD&A")

# List a report's sections
ds_sections(docs$id[1])
```

## Batch fetching

Fetch up to 31 documents in a single request:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- ds_batch(docs$id[1:5])
res$count   # number of documents returned
res$items   # list of document objects, each with full Markdown content
```

## Rate limits

The free tier is 3 requests/sec and about 8,000 reports per week; the yearly
tier ($31/year) is 31 requests/sec and 524,287 reports per week. See
<https://datasink.ing> for details.
